newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM says fears Peru hostage crisis accident.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM says fears Peru hostage crisis accident.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Monday expressed concern that an "unexpected accident" could occur as the 19-day-old hostage crisis in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima drags on.
"It will be a protracted battle, and situations like that make me worried about an unexpected accident," Hashimoto told reporters at his official residence.
"There have been miscues on the guerrillas' side and also on the the Peruvian government's side," he said without elaborating.
Hashimoto has firmly stressed since the outset of the hostage crisis that Tokyo wants a peaceful outcome and has also expressed fears that a dramatic rescue attempt could cause bloodshed.
Hashimoto, who cancelled New Year plans so he could monitor the hostage crisis, on Tuesday will begin a trip to five Southeast Asian countries.
The decision to go ahead with the trip signifies the premier's desire to not let the Peru crisis affect other diplomatic and political issues, Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda said.
"We will continue to place absolute trust in the Peruvian government and handle the crisis carefully," Ikeda said.
About 20 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas stormed a cocktail party attended by more than 500 people at the ambassador's residence on December 17.
The Marxist rebels released several hundred captives but still hold 74 VIP hostages. They are demanding the release of some 400 jailed comrades. Peru's President Alberto Fujimori has refused.
